title: Good work habits and gaining knowledge
intro: In Islam work is a kind of worship – and a child’s biggest job is learning.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah says that He created man to work hard and strive. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Balad 90:4)</small>

We get our first work habits in our family – we learn them from our mother and father. As we grow up with our parents or guardians, we see how hard they work to give us what we need. From them we learn that in life we should work and earn, and that way look after our own family.
In Islam, work is a kind of worship (ibadah) – a deed that Allah loves. Allah will reward us for our work and effort in this world and in the next.

Childhood is a very important time: we get ready for life and build the habit of working. Children should help their parents when they are asked, and also when they can see that their parents need help.

But our biggest duty is to learn and gain knowledge. What we will do in life depends on what we learn and how we do at maktab and school. Learning regularly gets us ready for life. If we do our maktab and school work on time, we build the habit of doing all our future duties on time too.

items: By spending time with friends our age, we learn to get along with people and make our first friends – often friends for life.

Playing together now and then makes friendships stronger. It is important to keep the rules of the game: rules get us used to the rules of life when we grow up. As Muslims we keep the rules Allah has given us, and as citizens we keep the laws people have made.

learn.title: 🚫 Beware of laziness!
learn.html: Laziness does not suit a Muslim. Muhammad (SAW) asked Allah to protect him from laziness.

If we want to be successful in this world and happy in the next, we should start every day with Fajr, and then do our work. Praying the five daily prayers teaches us to plan our day. It is important to do our duties on time, because then we will have more free time to play with our friends. Even more important is to keep to the Islamic way of behaving: doing what Allah has commanded or allowed, and staying away from what He has forbidden.

items.text: Doing homework as soon as you get home
Helping to clean the house without being asked
Leaving maktab homework until the last minute
Pretending to be asleep when Mom needs help

practice.title: A good day
practice.prompt: Put the day in a good order.
items: Do homework and help at home
Pray Isha and go to sleep

practice.title: Questions and tasks
prompts: 💬 How is work seen in Islam? What should we start our day with? What do the daily prayers teach us?
📋 Make your own table of your daily activities.
📚 Make a reading plan for one month – not counting school work and required reading – and put it somewhere you can see it. At the end of the month, reward yourself if you kept to your plan!
💬 Talk with your muallim about the saying: “Whoever works does not fear hunger!”
